Explicit contracts / no second renderer

A story that talks to your world.

Gameplay events enter the narrative engine. Story commands leave through registered handlers. This playground uses a simulated world; the bridge module is where you connect your real systems.

const story = new StoryEngine(project);
const bridge = new WorldworksStoryBridge({
  engine: story, bus, handlers
});
bridge.enterRegion('relay');
bridge.inventoryChanged('power_core', 1);
// Your existing loop — no extra renderer:
bridge.update(deltaSeconds, player.position);

Unhandled commands remain pending. A handler returns true only after it successfully applies a command. In multiplayer, run the engine and progression writes on the authoritative host.

 Worldworks / story system

Write it. Wire it. Play it.

Storyworks is a local branching-story editor and deterministic runtime. Choose a quest, edit a node, then restart the playtest to run the edited definition.

Click / drag a nodeSelect / arrange
Output dot → nodeConnect a branch to a target
Canvas drag / wheelPan / zoom around the cursor
F / NFit graph / add node
Ctrl/Cmd Z · Shift ZUndo / redo authoring
Ctrl/Cmd SExport authored project
Delete / EscapeDelete selection / cancel connection
Map: Shift + clickMove the test player into a trigger

Export project saves the story definition. Save in Playtest saves runtime progress, timers, event IDs, and the pending command outbox. Open either file to restore it; checkpoints must match the current story revision. Authoring drafts are saved locally when browser storage is available.

World bindings place cylindrical XZ triggers and interactable anchors. Import a Worldworks 0.1 project to preview its actual height field and asset IDs. This is a 2D binding map, not another Three.js renderer.

Demo hook handlers simulate doors, weather, reputation, effects, and rewards. They do not modify your other engine files. The included bridge module provides explicit input/output contracts and a Worldworks world+story bundle format.
